We build our own software, and we build other people's. Same standards either way.

A venture studio and product company with Southwestern roots. We research, design, build, launch and operate digital products — ours, and yours.

What we do

Our products

We start companies. StrideMap, NestEgg and Etch are ours — conceived here, built here, and still operated here. Each one began as a problem we wanted solved properly, and none of them was handed off to somebody else the week after launch. Running our own portfolio is what keeps the studio honest: we live with every decision long enough to find out whether it was a good one.

Yours

We take founders and businesses down the same road. Research what should exist, design it, build it, put it in front of real people, and stay on to operate it. We work in small numbers and go deep rather than wide. A product that ships and then quietly rots is not finished, so we plan for the second year before we write the first line.

How we work

Most of the cost in software is not the first version. It is the second year.

So we run a paved road: a written set of defaults that every product we own or build follows, whether it is a weekend tool or a company. It is the least glamorous thing about us and the reason our products are still standing.

01

One road, not one per project

Every product is stamped from the same template and runs the same stack — one repo, one documented set of hosts, one release process. Nothing boring gets decided twice, and anyone who has worked on one of our products can work on all of them.

02

Documentation written at build time

Every product ships the same set before it ships anything else: a README that actually gets you running, a privacy policy, an architecture note, a changelog in plain English, and a configuration contract listing every environment variable. Not requested later, when nobody remembers.

03

Secrets stay out of the repository

Public identifiers can ship in a binary. Everything else sits behind a proxy we control, with real values held by the host and never committed. It is the difference between a product you can hand over and one you have to babysit.

04

A maintenance rhythm, on the calendar

Dependencies reviewed monthly. A compatibility pass with every OS release. A portfolio view that says what is live, what is stale, and what needs a decision. Software rots quietly; the fix is a schedule, not good intentions.

Products

StrideMap

iOS · shipping

Every run you have ever taken, woven into one living map. StrideMap reads your whole running history out of Apple Health — Apple Workouts, Nike Run Club, Garmin, COROS, Polar, Strava, anything that writes a workout — and draws it as one accumulating web across the cities you have explored. Recent runs glow; older ones fade into the pattern. The point is not analytics. The point is where have I run.
